name: Shoebill stork
fact: A shoebill stands about 1.2 m tall and can stay motionless for hours waiting for lungfish.

name: Pink fairy armadillo
fact: The smallest armadillo: about 12 cm long and 5 cm tall. It lives in the sandy plains of central Argentina.

name: Okapi
fact: The giraffe's only living relative stands about 1.5 m at the shoulder and 1.9 m to the top of its head.

name: Moai statue
fact: The average Easter Island moai is about 4 m tall and weighs 12 tonnes. The tallest ever erected is nearly 10 m.

name: Zamboni ice resurfacer
fact: A full-size Zamboni is about 2.2 m tall, 4.5 m long, and tops out at 15 km/h.

name: Dodo
fact: The dodo stood about 1 m tall and weighed 10–18 kg. The last one was seen in 1662.

name: Trebuchet
fact: A large medieval counterweight trebuchet stood around 12 m tall and could hurl a 90 kg stone 300 m.

name: Tardigrade
fact: Tardigrades are about 0.5 mm long and 0.3 mm tall. They survive vacuum, radiation, and being frozen for decades.

name: Southern cassowary
fact: Cassowaries stand up to 1.7 m tall and have a dagger-like claw on each foot. They are often called the world's most dangerous bird.

name: Saiga antelope
fact: The saiga stands about 0.8 m tall. Its bulbous nose filters dust in summer and warms air in the Central Asian winter.

name: Naked mole-rat
fact: A naked mole-rat is about 4 cm tall and 10 cm long. It can live over 30 years and barely feels pain.

name: Sousaphone
fact: A sousaphone stands about 1.1 m tall with a 66 cm bell. It was designed in the 1890s so a tuba could be played while marching.

name: Antikythera mechanism
fact: The Antikythera mechanism was about 33 cm tall — a 2,000-year-old Greek gear computer for predicting eclipses, found in a shipwreck in 1901.

name: Terracotta warrior
fact: Each terracotta warrior is about 1.85 m tall. Some 8,000 of them guard the tomb of China's first emperor.

name: Stonehenge sarsen stone
fact: The sarsen uprights of Stonehenge's outer circle stand about 4.1 m above ground and weigh around 25 tonnes each.
